criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "States what the system is for and where it stands in 1 week, 1 quarter, 1 year and 5 years. Every horizon has at least one check an outsider could observe. It fits on one screen, meaning at most 300 words in vision.md."

Size: `wc -w charter/vision.md` gives 298 (265 if table pipes and other markup-only tokens are left out). Under the limit by 2 words on the stricter count.

Purpose: vision.md:7 states the north star ("Every surface keeps the same promises, whoever builds it") and lines 9-13 tie it to the seven principles and to universal, unified, scalable.

Horizons (vision.md:19-25), each with a check an outsider could observe in the repository or record:
- 1 day: every charter file has a fresh review and open questions are logged.
- 1 week: the four checkout parts pass their tests, and a less capable agent has built a checkout page from the docs alone.
- 1 quarter: the cost summary has been tested with people against a baseline (marked as needing a steward and participants).
- 1 year: three products use it, none bypasses the tokens, maintenance cost per product has fallen (the measure is defined as a proposal in DECISIONS.md A-09 and vision-notes.md:46 says it is "not measured" until two products exist).
- 5 years: a framework, build tool or model has been replaced without changing a principle's rule or a token name.

vision.md:17 says none has been met, so no result is claimed. vision-notes.md gives dated, fuller checks for each horizon and is consistent with the table.
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Already passes. Note the margin is 2 words on wc -w: any edit to vision.md must be re-counted.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "Five to seven contracts, ranked. Each has an 'A even over B' label, a rule, the evidence that shows it is kept, and the trigger that makes us act. Each can be failed by a concrete example. The six base values (universality, unity, scalability, honesty, longevity, removing the unnecessary) are all covered. The ranking settles every conflict between two principles."

Count and parts: seven numbered principles (principles.md:44-157). Each heading is an "A, even over B" label; each has Rule, Evidence, Trigger and "Breaks it" paragraphs with concrete failing examples (e.g. a pointer-only date picker; "Only 2 left" typed as text; a form that clears every field; two "primary buttons"; a fifth button variant; a token renamed with no alias; a core field with a "promo code" mode). The file says plainly (line 5) that no named check exists yet and Evidence is what will be collected.

Base values: coverage table at lines 163-171 maps universality 1, honesty 2, unity 4, removing the unnecessary 5, longevity 6, scalability 7; principle 3 is declared as an addition (A-07).

Ranking rule (lines 18-30) tested against concrete conflicts:
1. 1 against 2 (both LOCK): every mandatory charge and the estimate/generated markers must be shown before commit, yet the page must reflow at 320 pixels, 200% text and 40% longer translations. Text settles it: find the design that breaks neither or do not release; if none exists, principle 1 decides the design built, the conflict is logged, and the part stays unreleased until the steward rules.
2. 2 against 3 (both LOCK): the pay control must state the amount (3) while a charge is still unknown, so the amount would be untrue (2). Settled by the same paragraph: a design keeping both (no commit while a charge is unknown), else principle 2 shapes the unreleased design.
3. 1 against 3 (both LOCK): keep valid input after an error against values that must be dropped for security, and the no-re-entry accessibility row. Settled by worked case 1 and the matching security exceptions in both rows.
4. 3 against 5: a confirmation step against "less". Settled twice: a LOCK row "is never traded for anything", and worked case 2 limits when a separate confirmation is required.
5. 4 against 5: a product wants its own button variant. Settled: lower number shapes the design; "an addition to the system is better than a private copy", by the route in principle 5.
6. 6 against 7: composing with a web feature newer than 30 months. Settled: 6 shapes the design; the feature may only be an enhancement.
7. Performance budget against a LOCK row: an accessibility or safe-behaviour fix that needs script or CSS beyond a budget. Settled at line 28: the change is blocked and the budget goes to the CEO.
8. Performance budget against principles 4 to 7: three required themes or general composed parts pushing CSS over 12 or 2 kilobytes. Settled at line 28: budgets are hard checks, not traded by rank.

Every pair has a stated outcome: LOCK rules are never traded; LOCK against LOCK goes by number with the part unreleased; 4 to 7 go by number; budgets sit outside the ranking.
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Already passes. Two things would make the ranking tighter (see other findings): say in one sentence that the blocking L1 checks of principles 5 to 7 are constraints that rank cannot override, and give the 30-month rule in principle 6 its own evidence and trigger.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "Every LOCK item names the check that detects a breach. Every ADAPT item has a reference and a stated range. EXPLORE has an owner, a hypothesis, an expiry and a cap. The numeric performance budgets are stated."

LOCK, row by row (budget.md:31-84). All 33 rows name a check. Could it detect the breach?
- Accessibility (15 rows): text contrast, non-text contrast (declared pairs now include border and indicator colours), keyboard path, focus visible and not covered, target size, name/role/state/value (scan plus manual screen-reader check), autocomplete, live-region role, reflow at 320 and 200%, text spacing, colour alone (test now needs a difference in text, icon or shape, so a red-border-only error fails), right-to-left and 40% longer text, errors in text, no re-entry: yes for each. Reduced motion: yes for transitions only (see findings). Remaining WCAG criteria are assigned to a per-component audit in phase 3, which is a later item.
- Truthful content (6 rows, each split into what the system checks and what the product must declare): status, urgency wording, preselected extras, source markers: yes at the component and reference-page level. Full price before commit: partly (see findings). Label says what the control does: detects a missing verb or object, not a label that misdescribes.
- Meaning (4 rows): native element, token purpose, naming against the vocabulary file, no primitives (proven by a fixture using each group): yes.
- Safe behaviour (8 rows): consequence at the control, input survives error, no double action, destructive action by declared attribute, reversal control, no browser storage: yes. "Does not act on a guessed instruction" and standing permission: a reviewer's flow checklist, which the file states is "judged by review, not measured". Named and honest.

ADAPT (lines 109-119), nine rows, each with a Reference and an Allowed range column filled in. Could a script evaluate the range?
- Colour theme: yes. Accent and neutral (hue free, lightness and chroma fixed, 30 degrees from status hues): yes. Density (0.75, 1, 1.25): yes. Shape (multiplier 0 to 2): yes. Motion (at most 500 ms): yes.
- Typeface: yes for equal-width figures; language coverage only if the product declares its languages and ships font files.
- Line length: the 75-character ceiling yes; the 45-character floor "only where the container is wide enough" no.
- Layout: only once component contracts list arrangements (phase 3, a later item).
- Tone of voice: no, and the row says so ("Judged by review; the range check does not cover it").
The criterion asks for a reference and a stated range, which all nine have.

EXPLORE (lines 123-138): register entry requires owner, falsifiable hypothesis, start and expiry dates; expiry 30 days, extended once at most; cap of three active items and one new item per pilot or slice; a check on every change fails on an incomplete entry or a fourth item.

Performance budgets (lines 144-159): ten numeric rows (12 and 2 kB CSS, no required script, 5 and 15 kB enhancement script, 100 kB page, no blocking fonts, 2.5 s, 200 ms, 0.1, 200 ms), with the test profile and median-of-five rule. Byte figures are marked as unmeasured guesses to be reset at Gate 3.
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Already passes. The weakest rows are named in other findings: the full-price row needs a flow test on the reference page, the tone row needs a real range or a move out of ADAPT, and principle 4's bypass and duplicate checks need a stated class.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "A team model is chosen, with the alternatives and why they lost. A decision-rights table says who proposes, proves, decides and rolls back each kind of change. The passport is defined. Each of the four loops has its variable, current state, desired state, sensor, actuator, owner and cadence. The human like/dislike queue is defined."

Team model (operating-model.md:9-19): a central core team plus contributors is chosen. Solitary is rejected (fits one product; the CEO ruled out an ecommerce-only system), centralised is kept as the base with its risk named, federated is kept only as the contribution route (slow, split loyalties; Curtis's finding, which matches notes/survey/thinkers.md:14 and :57).

Decision table (lines 55-76): 20 rows; every row has all four columns filled. Every row has a decider (author, product, lead, steward, CEO, CEO and steward, or the gate reviewer). Roll-back is "Not applicable" only for passing a gate. The three gaps from run 1 are closed: adding a new part is now one row, always a promotion, decided by the steward (line 64); a breaking change with no real users has a row (line 61); changing a range in either direction goes to the CEO (line 73, logged as A-04 row 14).

Lead as proposer (line 78): proof is written by a fresh reviewer on Fable, the decision is the reviewer's verdict, the lead may not overrule it and may take a disagreement to the CEO. Covered.

Passport (lines 82-90): propose, prove, decide, with contents of each and the rule that the author of the first part never writes the third.

Loops (lines 98-108), all seven attributes present for each of L1 to L4: cadence ("Runs"), owner, variable, current state, desired state, sensors, actuator. Current states are honest: L1, L3 and L4 not running; L2 review running, benchmark and scans not.

Human review queue (lines 112-123): what enters, what the reviewer sees and does, who reviews, the outcome rule (three votes and a majority; 14 days), what it is not, and when it is built.
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Already passes as written. Two contradictions between the table and other text should be fixed before builders rely on it (see other findings): who decides a new variant, token or option, and who decides an EXPLORE item at expiry once the queue has reviewers.

otherFindings.where: Decision table line 60 ("a non-breaking change to a part": lead) against principles.md:115-121 and budget.md:125,138
otherFindings.problem: Principle 5 gives one route for any addition of a "component, variant, token, option and word": existing parts, then an EXPLORE item, then a second occurrence; its own breaking example is a fifth button variant. budget.md says promotion of an EXPLORE item is the steward's decision. The table only sends a new part down that route (line 64). Adding a variant, token or option to an existing part is a non-breaking change, so line 60 gives it to the lead with no EXPLORE step. The same change has two routes and two deciders. This is the remainder of the run 1 failure.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Add to line 60 "not an addition of a variant, token or option", and widen line 64 to "Adding a new part, variant, token or option outside the founding set". Or state in principle 5 that the route applies to parts only, and log that choice under Awaiting CEO.

otherFindings.where: Human review queue, lines 116 and 120, against table line 63 and budget.md:138
otherFindings.problem: The table and budget.md say the lead extends or retires an EXPLORE item at expiry, or proposes it for promotion. The queue says an EXPLORE item at expiry enters the queue and "anything else" than three votes with a majority of likes "is pulled back", including after 14 days with no vote. Once the queue has reviewers it is unclear whether the lead may still extend an item, or propose promotion without votes.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Say the queue vote is input to the lead's decision at expiry, or remove "an EXPLORE item at its expiry" from what enters the queue. State which rule applies before and after the queue has reviewers.

otherFindings.where: ADAPT table, "Tone of voice" row (line 119), with voice-and-tone.md:42
otherFindings.problem: The range is "as the tone table allows", but that table prescribes one tone per situation and gives no bounds on what a product may vary, so the effective range is unknown. voice-and-tone.md uses the ADAPT tag for something else ("ADAPT rules the lead may adjust"), which also conflicts with budget.md:107 and the decision table, where any change to a range needs the CEO. A product builder cannot tell what may vary or who approves it.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Either state what a product may vary in tone (for example which of the nine situations' shifts are fixed) or take tone out of the ADAPT table and say it does not vary by product. Rename the tag in voice-and-tone.md or align who may adjust it with the CEO rule.

otherFindings.where: Meaning table (lines 66-71) and "What zero drift means" (lines 163-167), against principles.md:18 and :109
otherFindings.problem: Principle 4 classes meaning and behaviour as LOCK, and principles.md:18 says those rules are LOCK rows in budget.md. The two central rules, no value that bypasses a token and no second version of something the system provides, have no LOCK row. They appear only as drift counts. Principle 4's trigger says "pull it back", not "release is blocked". A builder cannot tell whether a raw value or a duplicate component blocks release.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: State the class of each: add two rows to the Meaning table (bypass lint; duplicate scan, with its honest limits), or say they block merge in L1 but are not LOCK.

otherFindings.problem: The named system check is that the cost summary cannot render without a total and a list of charges. No named check asserts that a page with a committing control shows the summary before it, or that the amount at the pay control equals the summary total. A reference page that omits the summary, or adds a charge after the summary, would pass this row. The status row beside it does name a flow test on the reference pages; this row does not.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Add a flow test on the reference pages: the summary precedes the committing control, the amount at the control equals the summary total, and the amount the test server charges equals both.

otherFindings.problem: The rule that a web feature may be built on only after 30 months in every major browser, and that a newer feature may only add an enhancement, has no evidence and no trigger. The L1 scripts named cover only pre-release dependencies and renamed public names. This clause is a rule without a contract. Principle 7's "people and agents build from the same source" likewise has a trigger but no named sensor.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Name the evidence (for example a lint of CSS and HTML features against a dated support list) and the trigger for the 30-month rule, or mark it as enforced by review. Add a diff of the two generated doc sets as the sensor for principle 7.

otherFindings.where: Line 78, "When the lead is the proposer"
otherFindings.problem: Read literally, the sentence makes the reviewer's verdict the decision in every row the lead proposes, including running a pilot, a release to real users, and changes the table gives to the CEO. The bold rule above the table says otherwise, so the intent is clear, but the sentence is wider than it should be.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Begin it "In a row where the lead would both propose and decide,".

otherFindings.where: "How the ranking works", lines 22 and 28; triggers of principles 6 and 7
otherFindings.problem: For principles 4 to 7 "the lower number shapes the design", yet principles 6 and 7 have L1 checks that block a change regardless of rank, and budget.md gives 5 to 7 zero-delta entries. The text says budgets are not traded by rank but does not say the same for these checks. It also never states in one sentence that a rule of principles 1 to 3 beats a rule of 4 to 7; this is only implied by "never traded" and by the "strict priority" remark at line 191.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Add: "Blocking checks are constraints, whatever their principle's rank. Rank chooses among designs that pass them."

otherFindings.problem: It says the limits are "all" taken from an idea on the board. The board summary (notes/sources/2026-11-13-figjam-board.md:47, :118, :134) supports only one new item per pilot, and lists EXPLORE's expiry and cap as open questions. The three-item cap and the 30 days are the lead's own numbers.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Say which limit comes from the board (one new item per pilot, note N2) and that the other two were chosen by the lead.

otherFindings.problem: The length of the one allowed extension is not stated, so an item can be extended once by any amount. An item whose evidence needs people does not expire while waiting for a steward; with no steward named, such items have no working expiry. The file admits the second effect but not the first.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: State the extension length (for example another 30 days) and a review date for "waiting" items.

otherFindings.problem: Three checks are narrower than their rows. Reduced motion asserts only that no "transition" runs, which misses keyframe animation and scripted motion. The status flow test asserts that the status changes only after the server answers, not that it matches the answer. The label check (a verb and an object) cannot detect a label that names the wrong action.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Widen the first to "no transition or animation", make the second assert the state equals the server's answer, and add the label row to the reviewer's flow checklist.

otherFindings.problem: Three ranges cannot be fully evaluated by a script as written. Typeface: "covers the product's languages" needs a declared language list. Line length: "at least 45 only where the container is wide enough" has no test for wide enough. Layout: the allowed arrangements live in component contracts that do not exist until phase 3.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Require the language list in the theme file; drop the 45 floor or define the container width; note on the layout row that it is checkable from Gate 3.

otherFindings.problem: budget.md:15 and README.md:10 say each starting value is reviewed at the gate named beside it. Several have no gate beside them: the 2-pixel focus indicator, 0.01 seconds, 40% longer text, two releases, 30 months, below 1.0, three votes and 14 days. For those inside LOCK rows it is also unstated whether adjusting the number is a LOCK change needing the CEO and the steward.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Name the review gate for each, and say whether changing a starting value inside a LOCK row counts as a LOCK change.

otherFindings.where: Decision table line 72, against budget.md:142 and DECISIONS.md A-08
otherFindings.problem: The table gives every loosening of a performance budget to the CEO. budget.md and A-08 let the lead reset each byte budget once at Gate 3, up or down. The table does not carry that exception.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Add "except the one reset at Gate 3 (A-08)" to the row.

otherFindings.problem: D-006 says conflicts among the first three principles are "now settled without a person". principles.md:20 says the part stays unreleased "until the steward rules". Line 20 also names the steward alone, while line 183 says any LOCK change needs both the CEO and the steward.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Reword D-006 to "the design to build is settled without a person; release still waits for a person", and make line 20 name the same deciders as line 183.

otherFindings.problem: "Six are cited above" miscounts: seven of Rams' ten are cited (useful and understandable are two separate principles in notes/survey/thinkers.md:6), which with the three set aside makes ten. Separately, "a delivery fee that first appears on the final screen" does not break the rule as written if that screen comes before the committing action.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Change "Six" to "Seven". Reword the example to "a delivery fee that first appears after the person has committed", or tighten the rule if earlier disclosure is intended.

otherFindings.problem: "build from one source, without asking inside the written ranges until real users are affected" is hard to parse on first reading, in the one file meant to be read by everyone.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: "build from one source. Inside the written ranges they need no approval, until real users are affected." Re-count the words afterwards; the file is at 298 of 300.

summary:
Criteria 1, 2, 3 and 4 all pass as written. I judged the files as they stand, ran no git commands and wrote no files.

- **Criterion 1 (vision):** vision.md is 298 words by `wc -w`. It states the purpose and gives one observable check for each of the five horizons, with none claimed as met.
- **Criterion 2 (principles):** seven ranked contracts, each with label, rule, evidence, trigger and a breaking example; all six base values are covered. I tested the ranking on eight conflicts, including three pairs inside principles 1 to 3 and two involving the performance budgets, and the text gives an outcome for each.
- **Criterion 3 (budget):** all 33 LOCK rows name a check, all nine ADAPT rows have a reference and a range, EXPLORE has owner, hypothesis, expiry and cap, and ten numeric budgets are stated. Two ADAPT ranges cannot be evaluated by a script: tone, which the file admits, and the lower bound on line length.
- **Criterion 4 (operating model):** the team model and its alternatives are given, all 20 table rows have a decider, the lead-as-proposer case is covered, each loop has all seven attributes, and the queue is defined. The three gaps from run 1 are closed.

Six major findings sit outside the verdicts and should be fixed before builders rely on the charter:

1. **New variant, token or option:** the decision table gives it to the lead, while principle 5 and the budget route it through EXPLORE to the steward. This is the remainder of the run 1 failure on criterion 4; I passed the criterion because the table itself is now consistent and complete, and the conflict is between the table and principles.md.
2. **EXPLORE item at expiry:** the queue's automatic "pulled back" rule conflicts with the lead's right to extend or retire.
3. **Tone as ADAPT:** the tone row has no real range, and voice-and-tone.md uses the ADAPT tag with a different meaning and a different decider.
4. **Principle 4's class:** token-bypass and duplicate rules are called LOCK but have no LOCK row, so it is unclear whether they block release.
5. **Full price before commit:** no flow test checks that the summary precedes the pay control or that the amounts agree.
6. **Principle 6's 30-month rule:** it has no evidence and no trigger.

Eleven minor findings cover wording, provenance and narrow checks. One is a provenance overclaim: budget.md says all EXPLORE limits come from the board, but the board summary supports only one of the three.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "Every claim about how people behave is labelled as supported by cited research, inferred from established patterns, or an assumption that needs a human test. No result is invented. Targets come after baselines."

What holds. The five defects from run 1 are fixed: voice-and-tone.md:113 now sends a misreading to the steward with no pass mark; checkout-slice.md:112 is [pattern] and reports one tester; checkout-slice.md:111 dropped "Unexpected"; survey.md:75-76 are [P]; voice-and-tone.md:35 is [pattern]. Every [research]/[R] label matches its survey file with wording no stronger than the source: principles.md:72, checkout-slice.md:111 and survey.md:72 (Baymard 40%/12%, base and missing sample size stated; re-checked in the checkout-evidence.md review); survey.md:73 (Scott 2019; re-checked); survey.md:74 (11.3 fields, 42%) and survey.md:77 (GOV.UK start buttons) match checkout-evidence.md:15 and govuk-design-system.md:17, though neither line was among the claims the Opus review re-checked. No invented result found: scorecard "1 of 12" is shown by the review sections in notes/survey/ (only craft-and-taste.md has no corrections); every other cell is "no data yet". No target for people or for the benchmark is set before a baseline (principles.md:30, checkout-slice.md:91, benchmark.md:168). The performance budgets are numbers before measurement, but criterion 3 requires them, the byte budgets are marked as guesses reset at Gate 3, and the conflict is logged (A-04 row 10); I do not fail on them.

What does not hold: the first sentence. Claims about how people behave that carry none of the three labels:
1. operating-model.md:15-17, team-model table: "Fast; close to a real product", "Can lose touch with real products", "Slow; split loyalties", "No single product's agenda; consistent". These are claims about how teams of people behave. Line 19 cites Curtis via thinkers.md but gives no label, and "Fast" (solitary) and "consistent" (centralised) are not in notes/survey/thinkers.md:13 at all.
2. survey.md:55: "Developer complaints; one former engineer's account of weak adoption (anecdotes)". A claim about how developers (who are consumers of a design system) reacted, tagged "(anecdotes)", which is not one of the three labels. It is also stronger than its source: shopify-polaris.md:58 records one developer's forum post, not "complaints".
3. checkout-slice.md:122: "Asking from memory would test memory." An unlabelled claim about how participants respond, used to justify a measurement decision.
Secondary: voice-and-tone.md:35 quotes "40% gave 'extra costs too high'" without the base (shoppers who were not just browsing). Run 1 asked for the figure to be restated as principles.md:72 does; the base was left out, and the checkout-evidence.md review says the base "changes how the numbers can be read".

principles.md:40 and :66 set the same rule for the charter itself ("Every claim about how people behave carries a label"; "an unlabelled claim: ... the claim is removed"), so these are breaches by the charter's own standard, not only by the gate's.
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Four small edits. (1) operating-model.md:13-19: label the For/Against claims (for example [pattern: Curtis, notes/survey/thinkers.md]) and remove or separately label "Fast" and "consistent", which the survey file does not record. (2) survey.md:55: replace "Developer complaints" with what shopify-polaris.md:58 records (one developer's forum post) and give the row one of the three labels ([P] or [A]) instead of "(anecdotes)". (3) checkout-slice.md:122: add [assumption] to "Asking from memory would test memory" or fold it into the labelled assumption at line 117. (4) voice-and-tone.md:35: add the base of the 40% figure ("among shoppers who were not just browsing"), as principles.md:72 has it.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "Every conflict between the FigJam board and CLAUDE.md is logged under 'Awaiting CEO'."

The board summary (notes/sources/2026-11-13-figjam-board.md:139-148) lists eight conflicts. Each is a row of DECISIONS.md A-04, which sits under "## Awaiting CEO": decision rights inside ADAPT (row 1), the "A even over B" label (2), settled versus proposed status (3), no named steward (4, with A-02), the missing Retire exit (5), transfer to booking (6), the booking benchmark (7, with A-05), sync and telemetry (8).

I then read the "what we are proposing" block in notes/ceo-brief.md:464-598 against CLAUDE.md. The further differences it contains are also logged: "Gate 1: steward reads the charter" (row 9); "Steward picks one, or agent picks after a day" (row 11); "Ours: baseline first, targets after observation" against CLAUDE.md's numeric performance budgets in the charter (row 10); "Ours: baseline of people's outcomes" / "FIRST / Baseline ... Observe current task outcomes" with no earlier checkout to observe (row 12). The tagline's "Human agency", absent from CLAUDE.md's six base values, is logged separately as A-07. The build flow's retire path, the L1-L4 owners and cadences, the gaps list and the altitude note agree with CLAUDE.md.

Resolution follows the stated rule. Where real users or a LOCK are touched the board is followed: row 1 (any change reaching real users is the steward's, operating-model.md:53, repeated in budget.md:102 and vision.md:12), row 6 (evidence per part before transfer, checkout-slice.md section 6), row 9 (a Gate 1 pass does not make the LOCK rows firm; they stay provisional until the CEO reads them, README.md:5 and operating-model.md:80), row 12 (no target before the first measurement). Where neither is touched CLAUDE.md is followed (rows 2, 3, 7, 8, 10) or the two coincide (rows 5, 11). Rows 13 and 14 are charter-versus-CLAUDE.md points, logged in the same table.

Two wording differences are not logged; I judged neither a conflict that changes an outcome (see other findings): the board note "Components reference semantic tokens only" against CLAUDE.md's "semantic or component tokens only, never primitives", and the board's request for a human checkpoint on voice, on which CLAUDE.md is silent and which the charter adopts (voice-and-tone.md:116).
criteria.whatWouldMakeItPass: Already passes. To remove doubt, add two lines to A-04: one recording the board's "semantic tokens only" wording against CLAUDE.md's "semantic or component" and that CLAUDE.md's wording is used; one extending row 11 to voice, since the charter gives voice the same human checkpoint.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "A reader who has seen none of the work can follow the charter. Every special term is defined where it first appears or in charter/README.md."

Read in README order. The run 1 list is fixed (E1/E2 and H1/H2, the library, DTCG, APCA, MCP, llms.txt, human review queue, usage telemetry, word list, real user, pilot, core team versus core layer; NN/g, semver, Compose, "the admin" and the three designers in survey.md). The overall argument can be followed. The second sentence of the criterion is still not met.

Terms used but defined neither at first use nor in README.md:
- Used in the charter's own rules: WCAG (README.md:9 and 15 more uses; never expanded or described, although README defines APCA by reference to it); lint (principles.md:103, 18 uses); range check (budget.md:93, 102; operating-model.md:58) and register check (operating-model.md:62); alias (principles.md:137); consumer (principles.md:135); fresh / fresh-context review or reviewer (vision.md:21, vision-notes.md:26, operating-model.md:30); delta class (operating-model.md:86); primitive group and fixture (budget.md:71; "scenario fixture" is defined only at checkout-slice.md:11 and in a different sense); test server (budget.md:58, 79; explained only at checkout-slice.md:125); OKLCH and chroma (budget.md:112, benchmark.md:136); coarse pointer (budget.md:115); one-time key (budget.md:79); live-region role (budget.md:40); accessible name (used undefined inside README.md:52) and accessible description (benchmark.md:103); payload (operating-model.md:105); Lighthouse and gzip (budget.md:146, 157); viewport and touch emulation (benchmark.md:20, 143).

summary:
Gate 1, run 2, criteria 8 to 10: criterion 9 passes; criteria 8 and 10 fail, both on narrow grounds with small fixes.

Criterion 8 (honesty): fail. The five defects from run 1 are fixed, every [research] label matches its survey file, no result is invented and no target for people or the benchmark precedes a baseline. It fails on its first sentence only: three claims about how people behave carry none of the three labels (the team-model table at operating-model.md:15-17, where "Fast" and "consistent" are also absent from the cited survey file; "Developer complaints ... (anecdotes)" at survey.md:55, which is stronger than the one forum post its source records; "Asking from memory would test memory" at checkout-slice.md:122). voice-and-tone.md:35 also still quotes the 40% figure without its base. Four small edits would pass it.

Criterion 9 (conflicts): pass. All eight conflicts in the board summary and the four further differences in the "what we are proposing" block of notes/ceo-brief.md are logged in DECISIONS.md A-04 under "Awaiting CEO" (human agency is A-07), and each is resolved by the stated rule. Two unlogged wording differences do not change any outcome.

Criterion 10 (reader test): fail. The run 1 list is fixed and the argument can be followed, but "every special term is defined" is not met. WCAG, lint, range check, alias, consumer, fresh-context reviewer, delta class, primitive group, fixture and OKLCH are used in the charter's own rules with no definition; survey.md still carries about fifteen unexplained outside names; ADAPT, "tokens" and "usage" each carry a second meaning; and ten sentences could not be followed or read two ways.

One major finding outside the criteria: voice-and-tone.md:42 lets the lead adjust ADAPT-tagged voice rules, against the operating model's decision table. Ten minor findings cover a stale scorecard, three records that disagree on a count, unsourced outside facts and wording.

I did not read the tag v0.1.0-archive, ran no git commands and wrote no files. The retired AGENTS.md was present in my context, as DECISIONS.md A-01 describes, and I ignored it.

Parts (charter/checkout-slice.md): Field L26-32, Button L34-40, Feedback L42-49 and Cost summary L51-61 each have a Build line (states) and a Failures line. Feedback's Failures line, missing in run 1, is at L48. Every short LOCK name on L32, L40, L49 and L60 now matches a row in budget.md as it stands, including 44 pixels as ADAPT.

Comprehension: section 4 (L71-87) gives the setup, the stop point, four fixed questions, the answer key, per-question scoring, the pass rule and two independent scorers. No target is set: L91 "Targets are not set here", L127 "No target is set before it". A search of charter/ and scorecard.md found no numeric target for comprehension or the benchmark. The pass rule (all four correct) scores one person; it is not a group target.

Benchmark (charter/benchmark.md): all three prompts are written out in full (L52-63, L82-96, L116-130). The model, context, tools, limits, runs and order data are fixed (L13-44), and L3 says only the CEO changes the tasks after Gate 1. The prompts name no token, class, file or component of the system. "Compact", "square corners" and "light or dark" are options budget.md publishes (L111, L115, L116). An agent gets the prompt, docs, package, empty folder, shell and browser; nothing else is needed.

Arithmetic, recomputed: 2 x 24.50 = 49.00; 18.75; 3 x 3.25 = 9.75; subtotal 77.50; less 5.00 = 72.50; 8% = 5.80 exactly; plus 3.95 = 82.25. Items 14 + 13 + 14 = 41. Fifteen runs = 3 x 5.

Against budget.md and principles.md: Task 3 now varies only hue (budget L112), square corners are multiplier 0 set once (L116), compact is a listed step (L115), 3.10 is the 24 pixel LOCK and 3.11 the 44 pixel ADAPT value. The run-1 cause (a task that could not be met inside the accent range) is gone.

criteria.evidence:
Criterion: "Says what Souvenir sounds like, what it steers away from, and how tone shifts by situation. Its rules can be checked in review. It has examples for the four checkout parts."

charter/voice-and-tone.md:
- Sounds like: voice table, four traits each with a this-not-that pair (L9-14).
- Steers away from: seven items with examples (L16-24).
- Tone by situation: nine situations, each with the shift and an example (L28-38).
- Checkable rules: 17 numbered rules (L44-60). Most have a test a reviewer can apply to a string alone: the banned-word list (6), no exclamation marks (7), verb plus object and the forbidden labels (2), 20 words (10), word and sentence limits (11), full stop on messages only (1), same wording in field and summary (4), no "item(s)" (14). Every example row cites the rule numbers it illustrates.
- Examples for all four parts: Field L66-74, Button L76-84, Feedback L86-94, Cost summary L96-103.

The model strings that broke the file's own rules in run 1 now comply: errors end with a full stop, rule 3 no longer demands "what happened" when it is obvious, and rule 11 allows three sentences for a failure on our side. The example arithmetic is consistent: 48.20 less 3.99 is 44.21 (L102); 3.99 to 4.99 gives 49.20 (L103). The L3 row (L113) now sends a misreading to the steward and sets no pass mark.

Some cited rules do not actually catch their "Not this" string, and the ADAPT tag still has a second meaning. Neither stops a reviewer failing a string by rule number; both are under other findings.

otherFindings.where: "How items are tagged", last sentence (line 48); Scoring category 3 (line 157)
otherFindings.problem: "The rows of the Meaning table are checked by the count of values that bypass the system" does not match budget.md lines 66-71. The four Meaning rows are native element or role, token used for its stated purpose, one name per meaning, and no primitive tokens in components. A count of colour literals and numbers with units checks none of them; a page that references a primitive token directly has no literal and is not counted. No item carries a Meaning tag, so a Meaning breach never reaches the LOCK line. The scorecard would read as covering rows it does not check.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Say that the benchmark does not check the Meaning rows, which are left to the L1 lints, and that the bypass count measures principle 4's rule on values. Or add items tagged Meaning that test those rows.

otherFindings.problem: Item 2.5 is tagged Accessibility, so a failure counts as a LOCK breach. Its second half, "focus has moved to the first error or to a summary of the errors", is not a row in budget.md's Accessibility table and is not required by a WCAG 2.2 A or AA criterion. A page that announces its errors without moving focus can meet budget.md line 40 and still be scored as a LOCK breach. Run 1 listed 2.5 among the mis-tagged items; it was reworded but kept the tag. Smaller cases of the same kind: 2.2's "only" (a false error on a valid field is not an accessibility row) and 1.2 (line totals beside items are not in the full-price row).
otherFindings.suggestedFix: Split 2.5: "every error can be reached by keyboard" stays Accessibility; the focus move becomes its own item tagged P4 (follows the documented pattern). Retag the "only" half of 2.2 and item 1.2 to a principle. Do this before the tasks are fixed.

otherFindings.problem: ADAPT means two things. In README and budget.md it is a difference a product may make inside a written range, and changing a range needs the CEO. Here it marks a rule the lead may change. budget.md's tone row says a product varying its tone must still hold "the voice rules marked LOCK", which implies the ADAPT-tagged rules (sentence case, banned words, no exclamation marks, length) are optional for a product. Line 111 says the writing check blocks a change on banned words, case and length. A product writer cannot tell whether rule 7 binds them. Run 1 raised this and it is unchanged.
otherFindings.suggestedFix: State in line 42 that all 17 rules bind every product until changed, and that the tag only records who may change a rule. Use different words for that tag (for example "fixed" and "lead may revise"). Then correct budget.md line 119 to say what a product may vary: the tone table only.

summary:
Criterion 5 fails; criteria 6 and 7 pass.

**Criterion 5 (survey): fail, narrowly.** The adopt, adapt, avoid table exists, all twelve survey files carry a review section, and every run-1 defect is fixed. Three claims in charter/survey.md still say more than the file they cite, the same kind of defect run 1 failed on:
- Line 35: "none gives evidence" is not in craft-and-taste.md.
- Line 55: Material Web is given as a source for "deprecating before parity", but material-design-3.md says nothing about parity.
- Line 29: "None publishes DTCG JSON" is stated as fact; two files say only "could not find" and two are silent.

Three small edits fix it. Of the ten claims I sampled, eight were fully supported.

**Criterion 6 (checkout slice and benchmark): pass.** All four parts have states and failure states, and their LOCK names now match budget.md. Checkout comprehension is defined operationally and no target is set anywhere. The three prompts are written in full, name no internals, and the order arithmetic is correct (77.50, 72.50, 5.80, 82.25; 41 items). Task 3 now fits the accent, density and shape ranges.

Two scoring statements in benchmark.md still disagree with budget.md and are filed as major:
- Item 2.5 is tagged as an Accessibility LOCK breach for a focus move that budget.md does not require.
- Line 48 says the benchmark checks the Meaning rows; it does not.

Both are best fixed before the pass is recorded, because after Gate 1 only the CEO can change the tasks.

**Criterion 7 (voice and tone): pass.** Voice, steer-away list, tone by situation, 17 numbered rules and examples for all four parts are present, and the model strings now obey the file's own rules. One major finding: the ADAPT tag means something different here than in README and budget.md, so a product writer cannot tell which rules bind them.

Other findings: 3 major, 11 minor. I ran no git commands and wrote no files.
